data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense relies on a performative contradiction: it claims the preference is 'defensible' because it maximizes 'potential for learning,' yet simultaneously admits this offers 'no logical advantage' over random guessing if laws change. If there is no logical advantage to the better-corroborated theory regarding future performance (as the target concedes in its counterconditions), then the methodological rule cannot be rationally defended as superior to any other rule (including random selection) for the purpose of action. The target attempts to have it both ways: asserting the preference is rational/defensible while stripping it of the very predictive rationality that makes a preference defensible in an action-context.
